subject: Request: Residency certification + subprocessor escrow and DPA addendum
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@concord-healthcare.com>

Cc: procurement@concord-healthcare.com, dpo@concord-healthcare.com
Date: Sat, 18 Sep 2027 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Residency confirmation + subprocessor escrow process

Hi Priyom —

Thanks for the demo last week. As we evaluate Redwood for PII inference in our care coordination workflow, our legal and security teams need two pieces before procurement will move forward:

1) A firm, signed statement that Concord Health data will be pinned to US regions (primary deployment in US-EAST) with clear rules for any transient cross-border processing (allowed windows, TTL, logging).
2) A written process and evidence for how Redwood handles subprocessor turnovers and escrow for transient subprocessor keys or operator access (we need the roster and the escrow/litigation-contact process).

Could you share a DPA addendum or certification we can send to our security team and procurement? Also flag any items that would require a custom SOW or additional controls.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — procurement is targeting a signed contract by the end of next week.

Best,
Samantha Lee
Director of Security & Compliance
Concord Health

Hi Samantha —

Thanks — and great to hear procurement is on a fast track. We can provide both a DPA addendum that includes region-pinning commitments and an operations playbook for subprocessor escrow and turnover. High-level:

- Primary data hosting: US-EAST (us-east-1).
- Processing: User-level inference and embeddings will be routed to customer region by default.
- Transient cross-region processing: allowed only for short failover windows (default 72 hours) or for scheduled global batch jobs if explicitly enabled; both are logged and auditable.
- Audit evidence: per-request region metadata and audit logs retained for 13 months by default (can be adjusted per contract).

I'm looping in Marissa (legal lead on DPAs) and Kimberly (privacy/ops) to confirm the wording and share the actual addendum and subprocessor roster. Expect a draft within one business day.

Quick question for your team: do you require an on-premises key escrow (HSM) option or is a KMS-based escrow with customer-managed keys sufficient?

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Priyom —

We can produce an addendum that mirrors our standard DPA residency annex but with explicit language: primary region assignment (US-EAST), transient processing limited to documented failover windows up to 72 hours unless separately approved, and mandatory audit logging of region metadata. I recommend we offer two options in the addendum:

A) Standard: 72-hour transient failover window, KMS-based customer-managed keys supported, roster disclosure + 30-day notification for subprocessor changes.
B) Enterprise: HSM-based escrow option, 14-day notification, and extended audit log retention (24 months) for an enterprise addendum and pricing.

Kimberly — ops: can you attach the latest roster export and a short one-page escrow playbook? Rishi — please confirm whether we have any outstanding subprocessor contracts that would block disclosure.

I'll prepare a draft addendum (template) named Redwood_DPA_Addendum_Residency_v1.2.pdf and a companion operations document Redwood_Subprocessor_Escrow_Process.pdf for Concord to review. I will also mark the 72-hour window as negotiable in the addendum (we can add language: "transient processing permitted only for the reasons specified in Section X and limited to 72 hours unless otherwise agreed").

Marissa
Associate General Counsel
Redwood Inference

Hi Samantha —

Attached are the documents Marissa and Kim prepared: Redwood_DPA_Addendum_Residency_v1.2.pdf (DPA addendum with both Standard and Enterprise options), Redwood_Subprocessor_Escrow_Process.pdf (one-page ops playbook), and the current subprocessor roster (CSV). Highlights:

- Residency pledge: Primary processing will occur in US-EAST (us-east-1); we commit to region metadata tagging for each request and per-request logging.
- Transient cross-region processing: Standard option limits transient processing to 72 hours for failover events; explicit exceptions (longer windows or scheduled cross-region batch jobs) require written customer approval and will be scoped in an SOW.
- Keying/escrow: KMS-based customer-managed keys are supported in Standard; Enterprise supports HSM-based escrow at an additional cost and integration scope.
- Notification timeline: Standard: 30 days for non-material subprocessor additions; Enterprise: 14 days.

If this looks good to you, Marissa has added a DocuSign link for the Standard addendum (no pricing change) — you can sign online and procurement can attach it to the master SOW. If you prefer Enterprise terms we can route to pricing and a short SOW addendum.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/envelope/ABC123-REDWOOD-CONC
Drive (evidence): https://drive.redwood.internal/drive/Shared/Residency_Addendum_v1.2

Let me know which option Concord prefers and whether you need any additional operational evidence (server certificates, SOC-2 control mappings, sample audit log excerpts).
